prompt: The interior of a Victorian detective's office in London, lit by a crackling fireplace and a single candlestick on the desk. The large wooden desk is cluttered with clues: a magnifying glass lies on an open case file, next to a tobacco pipe and a smudged newspaper. A detailed map of London is pinned to the wall above the fireplace. A leather armchair is angled toward the desk. On a side table, a whiskey decanter stands next to a half-full glass tumbler. An old inkwell and a fountain pen are neatly arranged. The detective's iconic deerstalker hat rests on a coat stand. A violin in its case leans against a bookshelf filled with criminology texts and a human skull. On the mantelpiece, there's a small chemistry set and a recently arrived telegram. A worn Persian rug covers the floor. An evidence bag made of cloth sits on the corner of the desk, beside a heavy revolver and a gold pocket watch. The setting is authentic to the era, so it is free of modern items. There is no computer, no humming fluorescent light, no plastic chair, and certainly no mobile phone or electric coffee machine.
